english: he who says what he likes will hear what he does not like

terms.latin: Sī mihi pergit quae volt dīcere, ea quae nōn volt audiet.
terms.comment: Literally “if he goes on saying what he likes to me, he will hear what he does not like”: Terence’s threat, which the proverb generalizes.

terms.latin: Quī quae vult dīcit, quae nōn vult audiet.
terms.comment: The proverb made from Terence’s line.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Terence, Andria 920, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (12 November 2026).
